root_cause: The Radios component only listens for click and change events within its own module. When radio buttons sharing the same name are split across multiple modules (as in the test), a keyboard-driven selection change in one module does not trigger conditional updates in the other module, leaving the now-irrelevant conditional field visible.
repair_strategy: Extend each Radios instance to also listen for 'change' events on the document for radio names that have associated conditionals (aria-controls) within its module. When such a change occurs anywhere in the document, update the conditionals for all radios in this module with that name and aria-controls.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate among radio options across module boundaries using arrow keys and see dependent fields appear/disappear correctly, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.4.3 Focus Order, and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.
functional_risks: Document-level change listeners are added per Radios instance; if many instances exist for the same name, duplicate listeners may fire but setAttributes is idempotent.
The change listener triggers on any radio with the same name, even those not in a Radios module, but the guard condition ensures only relevant inputs are updated.
verification_requirements: Verify that arrow key navigation from Text message to the opt-out answer hides the mobile number field.
Verify that arrow key navigation from Email to Text message shows the mobile field and hides the email field.
Verify that clicking radios with mouse continues to work as before.
Verify that the form's reflected value matches the selected radio after keyboard interaction.
Ensure no regression in existing automated tests for the radios component.
